outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Crisis of Scaling and the Promise of Extreme Quantization
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by examining the growing challenges of deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) due to their massive size, memory footprints, and energy consumption. It introduces the concept of quantization as a solution and contrasts post-training quantization techniques with the architecture-level innovation proposed by BitNet b1.58. The chapter argues for a paradigm shift from merely reducing bit-width for inference to redefining the fundamental arithmetic operations used in model training and deployment.
subtopics: The computational and environmental limits of current LLM scaling.
Post-training quantization (PTQ): Techniques like GPTQ and AWQ and their limitations.
The bottleneck of floating-point arithmetic (FP16/BF16) in matrix multiplications.
The historical context of low-bit models and the difficulty of training 1-bit models.
Introduction to BitNet: Moving from weights-only quantization to architecture-level ternary representation.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: The BitNet b1.58 Architecture: Design Principles and Mechanics
outline.description: This chapter provides a deep technical dive into the architecture of BitNet b1.58. It explains how the model replaces standard linear layers with 'BitLinear' operations, detailing the mathematical formulation of the ternary weight space {-1, 0, 1}. It covers specific architectural choices such as the `absmean` quantization function, activation handling, and adoption of LLaMA-style components to ensure broad compatibility with existing software ecosystems.
subtopics: The computation paradigm: Replacing FP MUL/ADD with INT ADD/LOOKUP.
Mathematical definition of Ternary Weights: From 1-bit to 1.58 bits.
The `absmean` Quantization Function: Scaling strategies and round-clip mechanics.
Activation Quantization Strategies and avoiding zero-point complexity.
Architectural Compatibility: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, Rotary Embeddings, and Bias removal.
Breaking biases in LLaMA for pure ternary implementation.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Evaluation Methodology and Experimental Setup
outline.description: This chapter details how BitNet's performance claims are validated. It outlines the training data (RedPajama), token counts comparisons, and evaluation datasets used for both perplexity (wikitext2, C4) and end-task accuracy (ARC, HellaSwag, etc.). It also describes the infrastructure used for latency, memory footprint, energy estimation, and throughput measurements to ensure a fair comparison against FP16 baselines.
subtopics: Training Regimen: Data sources (RedPajama), tokenizer alignment, and token counts.
Downstream Evaluation Tasks: Language modeling benchmarks vs. discrete classification tasks.
Inference Benchmarking: GPU memory usage (FasterTransformer integration).
Latency Metrics: Time per output token analysis.
Throughput Analysis: Batch size scaling on specific hardware (A100).
"Training Tokens" Equivalence: Comparing a smaller bit model vs. larger FP models.
